author: Guardian Staff
description:
The 20th Asian Games are on in Japan’s Aichi Prefecture and the city of Nagoya, from 19 September to 4 October. About 11,000 athletes from 45 countries are competing across 43 sports

title: The 20th Asian Games, from Nagoya, Japan – in pictures

author: Uwa Ede-Osifo and Robert Mackey
description:
US president doubles down on criticism of CNN and MS Now as Akayla Gardner questions attempted White House ban

A day after the White House barred CNN from traveling aboard Air Force One to provide pool television coverage of the president’s trip to Tennessee, Donald Trump doubled down on his criticism of that broadcaster and another, MS Now, he has attempted to ban over coverage of him he calls overly negative.

As he left the White House early on Saturday, Trump was asked by MS Now White House correspondent Akayla Gardner: “Do you only want outlets that support you to be a part of the press pool?”

Continue reading...
title: Trump tells female MS Now reporter to ‘be quiet’ amid questions on press pool ban

author: Pablo Iglesias Maurer at Inter&Co Stadium
description:
• Eleven players make US debuts in Orlando

  • Sullivan, 16, starts in youngest US appearance in years

  • Ellis and Hall score as Pochettino’s new faces impress

Playing in their first match of the 2030 World Cup cycle, the US men’s national team crushed Peru 4-1 in at Orlando’s Inter&Co Stadium on Saturday, riding goals from newcomers Justin Ellis, Zavier Gozo and Justin Hall to victory. The win marked the US debut of 16-year-old Philadelphia Union midfielder Cavan Sullivan, whose appearance in the US starting XI makes him the youngest player to feature for the national team in over two decades.

Sullivan received the lion’s share of the attention in the lead-up to Saturday’s match but it was Orlando City’s Ellis who stole the show early, nodding home a Gio Reyna free kick in the fourth minute to give the US an early lead. Playing in his home stadium, Ellis himself was involved in the build-up that led to the free kick, part of
title: USA thrash Peru as teenage newcomers shine in first step toward 2030

author: Compiled by Michael Williams
description:
More than 200 cats came to compete in the Romania International Cat Show, an international feline beauty contest known as the Feline Oscars, in Bucharest

Continue reading...
title: Paws for applause: the Feline Oscars – in pictures

author: Evonne Goolagong Cawley
description:
As a teenager in Sydney, the would-be Wimbledon champion was working towards a singular goal when an act of racism shattered her naivety

It was a regular match. Until it wasn’t. In 1969, I was 17 and had been living in Sydney with my tennis coach, Vic Edwards, and his family for several years. I had left my home town of Barellan – on Wirajudjuri country in the Riverina region of New South Wales – to pursue my tennis dreams in the big smoke.

The year before, I had finished high school at Willoughby girls high – where I was the only Aboriginal student – and I was doing my secretarial course in the city. The Metropolitan Business College where I studied was conveniently located near the headquarters of the Foundation for Aboriginal Affairs.

Continue reading...
title: I was focused on becoming the first Aboriginal tennis champion. Then one remark changed something in me

author: Jeff Rueter
description:
• USA v Peru kicks off at 4.30 ET

  • Cavan Sullivan, other young players could make debuts

  • Sign up for our free newsletter for US readers

  • Email Jeff with thoughts, questions and jokes

A quick note on Cavan Sullivan’s debut; he becomes the fourth-youngest player to feature for the USMNT, behind Freddy Adu and a couple of unheralded teenagers, Mike Slivinski and Mark Jonas. The latter two were unknown high school players when they featured for the US in a 1991 friendly against Jamaica.

Sliviniski actually debuted in US head coach Bora Milutinovic’s XI in the US
title: USMNT v Peru live – analysis and updates from international friendly in Orlando

author: Jonathan Wilson
description:
When things are going awry, the Albiceleste will no longer be able to rely on their ultimate get-out clause

It isn’t quite over yet. Lionel Messi will return a week on Wednesday for his formal farewell in a friendly against Benin, but, before that, Argentina face two games when they will begin to experience a future without the most potent get-out-of-jail-free card football has known.

Messi’s international career falls into two distinct halves. There was the first decade when there was a sense that he didn’t quite fit, was somehow insufficiently Argentinian, didn’t care for his country. That was always absurd and can be recognised now as a manifestation of the Argentinian public’s frustration at their trophy drought despite the presence in their forward line of one of the best three to play the game.

Continue reading...
title: Messi’s exit leaves Argentina with impossible task of replacing their superhero | Jonathan Wilson

author: Agencies
description:
• Air Force One flies low over Neyland before kickoff

  • Schools coordinate with Secret Service over headsets

  • Fans urged to arrive early amid enhanced screening

Encouraging fans to get inside Neyland Stadium earlier than usual with Donald Trump coming to Tennessee’s college football game against Texas sure worked Saturday.

Security checks on the stadium’s perimeter went relatively smoothly with Tennessee officials opening the stadium 30 minutes earlier than normal. Fans got half-price off concessions as a reward for showing up early, and Tennessee faithful had the stands half full 90 minutes before kickoff and nearly packed an hour before.

Continue reading...
title: Trump flyover and Secret Service checks greet fans at marquee Texas v Tennessee clash

author: Helena Smith in Athens
description:
Emergency teams discovered victims after two-storey building in historic Plaka district collapsed ‘in a matter of seconds’

Greek authorities say they are trying to discover what caused a two-storey apartment block in the heart of ancient Athens to collapse “in a matter of seconds”, killing six people.

Emergency teams found the victims, including four American tourists, on Saturday, more than 24 hours after an explosion prompted the early morning tragedy in the historic Plaka district.

Continue reading...
title: Greek authorities seek answers after six killed in Athens apartment block explosion

author: Pippa Crerar political editor
description:
Exclusive: UK prime minister says delivering fiscal stability would be ‘crucial’ to be able to fix bigger problems

Andy Burnham has said he can deliver on his promise of radical change for the country despite severe economic headwinds, telling the Guardian: “There’s always things you can do, it’s just whether you’re prepared to do them.”

The prime minister acknowledged the public finances were “challenging” ahead of next month’s budget but said that delivering fiscal stability would be “crucial”, because only then would the government be able to focus on fixing bigger problems.

Continue reading...
title: ‘I can deliver’: Burnham pledges radical change on eve of Labour conference

author: Chloe Mac Donnell
description:
With Jennifer Lopez providing some star power, the Italian house’s Milan show came at a crucial time for the brand

Earlier this week Jennifer Lopez walked down the Vogue World catwalk in Milan wearing a black beaded A-line bustier dress from Dolce & Gabbana. On Saturday, she sat in the front row at the Italian house’s womenswear show in a three piece velvet suit from the same brand, her look topped off with a baker-boy cap.

The reminder of Dolce & Gabbana’s inimitable celebrity connection is no coincidence. In a turbulent luxury market, the brand has found itself trying to navigate a nearly £400m debt pile.

Continue reading.
title: Dolce & Gabbana mixes it up as pressure mounts for turnaround

author: Geraldine McKelvie
description:
Alexander Millington-Cotes is concerned for welfare of the 82-year-old, who hasn’t been seen in public for two years

The stepson of Sir Ranulph Fiennes has launched a crowdfunder to pay for “specialist legal advice” in an attempt to locate the explorer, who hasn’t been seen in public for more than two years.

Alexander Millington-Cotes, 31, has set a target of £55,000 for the fundraiser, to enable him to instruct lawyers to “locate and safeguard” Fiennes.

Continue reading...
title: Ranulph Fiennes’ stepson appeals for funds to ‘locate and safeguard’ the explorer

author: Giles Richards
description:
• Briton forced to retire from Azerbaijan GP when eighth

  • Colapinto given a grid drop at the next round in Malaysia

Lando Norris has issued a scathing criticism of Franco Colapinto, saying the Alpine driver does not deserve to be in Formula One and should face a ban after taking Norris’s McLaren out of the race.

The Azerbaijan Grand Prix was won by Mercedes’ George Russell but Norris was forced to retire from eighth place after Colapinto caused the accident that all but ended the defending world champion’s title hopes.

Continue reading...
title: Lando Norris says Colapinto ‘shouldn’t be in F1’ after crash ends title hopes

author: Ramon Antonio Vargas
description:
Authorities discovered a body hidden in a home’s crawlspace in 2020, 13 years after Jill Maiorca disappeared

A man was recently charged in California with the killing of his ex-wife six years after her remains were discovered in a crawlspace beneath a home – and about two decades after when she went missing, according to investigators.

Jeff Maiorca, 53, faces a charge of murder in the death of Jill Maiorca, who was 29 when she was killed, authorities said in discussing what could be one of the latest cases in the US to be solved with modern DNA techniques.

Continue reading...
title: California man charged in the killing of his ex-wife – two decades after she vanished

author: Ewan Murray at the Stadion Stozice
description:
Sébastien Pocognoli grimaced on Friday when recalling his playing debut for Belgium. Alessandro del Piero and Italy discovered favourable opposition when preparing for the 2008 World Cup. Pocognoli will also look back, in time, at his maiden game as the head coach of Scotland. Blue skies, a dainty stadium in Ljubljana and a second half display that provided glimpses of optimism in respect of Scotland’s world post-Steve Clarke. The best-forgotten first 45 minutes can be explained by a squad operating under a new regime. By full-time, Slovenia were grateful for their point. Scottish players took deserved applause.

Scotland’s failing here was a familiar one. A lack of goals haunted Clarke. This version of Scotland did at least create a handful of openings. Scott McTominay, a key attacking threat, was missing. Instilling ruthlessness in a team is no easy task but it is one Pocognoli has the coaching credentials to meet. Slovenia, on this evidence, have the more significant challe
title: Pocognoli’s reign as Scotland coach begins with stalemate in Slovenia

author: Kevin Rawlinson and agency
description:
BBC broadcaster was shot in 1999 in case detectives have previously said may never be solved

Technological advances are allowing police to review old CCTV footage in the unsolved murder of the BBC broadcaster Jill Dando, Scotland Yard has revealed.

Advances in CCTV enhancement technology have allowed detectives to return to 27-year-old footage of Putney Bridge Underground station, Scotland Yard said. But detectives stressed that the review was part of existing inquiries – not a new investigation.

Continue reading...
title: Jill Dando murder: technological advances allow police to review CCTV 27 years later

author: Jack Snape
description:
With Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii on the wing and a bench packed with forwards, coach Les Kiss is hoping he has a formula to topple the Springboks

The weight of the occasion is almost enough to tip the great red continent into the Indian Ocean. Sunday night’s clash between the Wallabies and South Africa in Perth marks a year from the start of the home World Cup, which will kick off with the Wallabies playing at the same venue.

The date with the mighty Springboks is also the first match under Wallabies coach Les Kiss against one of the traditional rugby powers. It’s also the country that happened to give the Australian his first opportunity coaching in union more than two decades ago.

Continue reading...
title: Wallabies gear up for mouthwatering South Africa clash: ‘A massive, massive Test’ | Jack Snape

author: Luca Ittimani
description:
Sam Altman and Dario Amodei have been invited to appear before the Greens-led inquiry into AI and datacentres

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

The chief executives of OpenAI and Anthropic have been called to face a Senate inquiry after rogue OpenAI agents hacked Australian and US government websites.

Sam Altman and Dario Amodei were requested to appear at the Greens-led inquiry into AI and datacentres as their companies negotiate with the Labor government for greater access to Australian content in exchange for a greater local presence.

Sign u
title: Heads of OpenAI and Anthropic called to face Senate inquiry after rogue agent incidents

author: Edward Helmore
description:
Beth Macy, author of Dopesick, is drawing on her reporting experience to win Virginia voters in a longtime Republican district

Virginia’s sixth congressional district has been in Republican hands for over 33 years, but Beth Macy, a longtime reporter with the Roanoke Times and author of Dopesick, a powerful account of the opioid crisis that swept through Appalachia two decades ago, has a plan to change that.

The plan, drawing on her experience as a reporter, is to canvass the district in the mountainous west of the state, knocking on doors, going to food pantries, meeting with veterans. It’s what any political hopeful might do, but with a twist: Macy carries her reporter’s notebook and jots down the good stories she’s been told.

Continue reading...
title: ‘I’m not JD Vance’: the Appalachia memoir author running for Congress

author: Associated Press
description:
Thousands already without without power as New Jersey, Massachusetts, Delaware and New York brace for nor’easter

More than 70,000 customers were without electricity in the north-eastern US on Saturday, a major sign of a powerful storm known as a nor’easter that was expected to create dangerous conditions through the weekend.

Forecasters warned of gale winds that could down trees and heavy inundations that could flood roads.

Continue reading...
title: Power outages and flooded roads as major storm bears down on US north-east

description:

Sebastien Pocognoli: “We had a good camp, we reached all the aspects that we wanted to reach on the pitch but also off the pitch,” said Scotland’s head coach during his press conference at the Stozice Arena.

“Regarding the first game for Scotland, I’m excited because we want to see what we worked on this week. I’m very curious to see if we can produce this. I hope we are well balanced, well focused and well concentrated in the good moment, but also in the challenging moments.

author: Associated Press
description:
Human rights council names and shames businesses with ties to illegal Israeli settlements in West Bank

The UN human rights office has added 61 more companies to a blacklist of firms that it says are involved in violating Palestinian human rights through business ties to Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank.

The vast majority of the total 214 companies, which are based in 11 countries, are Israeli. Five of the 158 companies listed last year were removed in the latest update.

Continue reading...
title: UN adds 61 companies to settlements blacklist over alleged Palestinian human rights violations

author: Ethan Penny and Dan Milmo
description:
University staff voice concerns over reputational risk of partnering with company behind ChatGPT

The University of Oxford has allowed the company behind ChatGPT to train its AI models on historical texts from its Bodleian Library, as tech companies scour academic institutions for fresh data.

The Bodleian material digitised by OpenAI has been used to “populate the OpenAI training set”, according to internal documents.

Continue reading...
title: Oxford lets OpenAI train its AI models on Bodleian Library

author: Gaya Gupta in Bangor, Maine
description:
President’s tariffs have hurt fishers, loggers and others in a state with deep bonds to Canada – will voters show their displeasure in the midterms?

It was an ideal summer to cut trees.

The weather in Maine’s Penobscot county – one of the most heavily forested counties in a state dense with trees – was warm and dry. Yet even as the county’s wood had grown to an ideal size to harvest, the machines Molly London typically uses sat idle.

Continue reading...
title: ‘It’s just getting worse’: anger in Maine over Trump’s trade war with close neighbor Canada

author: Jake Jackson; as told to Olivia Ladanyi
description:
I had always ignored my anguished mental state or tried to push it aside, and CBT didn’t work for me – then one song seemed to articulate my pain

Six months ago, I was driving past John Lewis on the M40 with my wife and stepdaughter, Raye’s I Know You’re Hurting playing on the stereo, when I realised I was crying. It was the third time I’d listened to the song, but it was the first time I’d really heard it. It was as though the lyrics were speaking directly to me: “I can see you standing on the edge … You give when you have little left to give.”

Music had made me emotional before, but only ever because of the melody or the arrangement or the orchestration. I have worked in music since I was 21, and as a recording and mix engineer, I’ll listen to a song all day, taking it apart to work out how to make it better. After listening to a song 200 times, it inevitably loses its meaning, and over the years, I’ve become desensitised to the power music can have. But this time, fo
title: Raye’s I Know You’re Hurting urged me to confront a lifetime of depression

author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen  and Aakash Hassanin Tarluvada
description:
Locals say Google’s $15bn project in Andhra Pradesh has resulted in smallholdings being taken back off them by the government

When the government officials arrived in Tarluvada last year, they came with abundant promises.

Google, one of the world’s richest and most powerful tech companies, would soon be bringing a “golden opportunity” to this tiny village in south India: a $15bn AI datacentre.

Continue reading...
title: Broken promises, confiscated land: the hyperscale AI datacentre being built in a tiny Indian village

author: Steve Rose
description:
Ten years ago, the San Francisco 49ers quarterback refused to stand for the national anthem. He was accused of disrespecting the flag, the game, and America. In a rare interview, he talks about inspiring a global gesture of civil rights

Colin Kaepernick still gets up at 4.30am every morning to train. “Strength training, speed training, position training – still do all of the same type of workouts I did while I was playing,” he says cheerily. “And then go about the rest of my day.” It is almost 10 years since Kaepernick last played a game of top-flight football. His career was abruptly and cruelly cut short just as it was peaking, after the National Football League (NFL) effectively closed ranks and shut him out for being too political. Now, at 38 years old, he is well aware that his chances of a return are dwindling by the day, but he remains as game-ready as ever. “I stay relentless at it,” he continues in his easy drawl. “I look at it from the perspective of, ‘What are the
title: ‘Refusing to meet Trump was an easy no’: Colin Kaepernick on being ‘blackballed’ for taking the knee, racism, and why he’s still ready to play

author: Vaughan Tomlinson
description: Continue reading...
title: Vaughan Tomlinson on billionaires and their kids – cartoon

author: Staff and agencies
description:
Tehran awaits official response to plan, but US president is said to expect renewed strikes after midterms

Iran is ⁠awaiting an official US response to its proposal to reopen the strait of Hormuz and end fighting in the Middle East war as Donald Trump was reported to have rejected the deal.

Iran raised the diplomatic initiative at the UN general assembly in New York, saying it had been transmitted ⁠to the Americans via Qatari mediators and could ⁠reopen the strategic waterway and put an end ​to hostilities in the region within seven days.

Continue reading...
title: Trump reportedly rejects Iran’s seven-day peace deal to reopen strait of Hormuz

author: Nathan Kalman-Lamb, Simran Kaur Sethi and Derek Silva
description:
Aminata Seck’s detention shows the bargain facing international college athletes: universities eagerly recruit them, but support can disappear when their immigration status becomes precarious

Earlier this week, news broke for the first time that Senegalese Division II Kentucky State women’s basketball player Aminata Seck was abducted by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) at Louisville’s Muhammad Ali International Airport on 7 August during a trip to attend the HBCU All-Star game in New York. Seck is listed as a Kentucky State senior and last year started 20 of 26 games, earning third-team all-conference honors and an SIAC Elite 16 award for academic achievement.
title: ICE has abducted a college athlete. What are the NCAA and universities going to do about it?

author: Andy Hunter
description:
• Club’s owners FSG move swiftly to fill key post

  • Move comes amid upheaval in Anfield hierarchy

Liverpool have appointed Julian Ward as their sporting director for a second time following the departure of Richard Hughes to Al-Hilal.

Ward, who was Liverpool’s sporting director for one season in 2022-23, has returned to the role after spending the past two years as technical director for Fenway Sports Group, the club’s owners.

Continue reading...
title: Liverpool rehire Julian Ward as sporting director to replace Richard Hughes

author: Sarah Marsh Consumer affairs correspondent
description:
As Britain goes mad for yam, shortage of planting material and concerns over control of crop prompts sales halt

In a corner of north London on a weekday morning, Filipino cuisine is thriving: diners at Mama & Sons in Kentish Town are making their choices, and one of the most popular items on the menu is the ube ice-cream sandwich. It’s easy to see the appeal of the light, fluffy bun encasing a purple scoop of ice-cream.

The owner of the cafe, Omar Shah, says ube – a vibrantly purple root vegetable long-beloved in the Philippines – has exploded in popularity in the UK. Just when he thinks it has reached its peak, it becomes “even more popular”. And this year, he says, has been no exception.

Continue reading...
title: Purple reins: Philippine export ban casts shadow over UK’s love of ube

author: Suzanne Wrack
description:
She left her Indian Ocean island home at the urging of Chelsea’s now-manager – now they’re working together again in pursuit of a Stamford Bridge legacy

It is rare to see Melvine Malard without a grin and she has a mountain of reasons to keep it that way. A wedding in June, a big-money move to Chelsea, a Ballon d’Or nomination and a first taste of a fiery London derby against Arsenal at Stamford Bridge on Sunday. The French forward is loving life and the personality behind the smile that instantly connects her to teammates is infectious.

“Goals,” says Malard, with a laugh, when asked what keeps her happy. “Seriously though, it’s seeing the kids, the families, my family, in the stands. It is crazy. I love my life, I love my job, I’m happy with my wife and everything is good. I smile because of those things, because I’m happy.”
title: ‘Island girl’ Malard aims to ‘become a legend’ in Réunion with Bompastor

author: Sid Lowe
description:
Spain and Barcelona wonderkid has won World Cup and European Championship but says there are no limits for his career

Like the kid he is, Lamine Yamal just wanted to keep playing. This wasn’t Plaça Joan XXIII, wasn’t El Parque de Rocafonda either; it wasn’t the Mataró neighbourhood where it all began, but it might have been. “We’re in a World Cup final and I wanted to carry on,” he says, and there’s the smile again, the braces. Really? “Yes”. No nerves? “No. I never thought: ‘Just blow the whistle’. I was enjoying it.” No fear, just fun: 19 July, New Jersey and he knew: this 19-year-old who had happily been asleep on the bus to the biggest match of his life.

And now he sits in a first-floor office in Las Rozas, surrounded by tactics boards and stats sheets. There’s a Spain keyring hanging from the door and a second star on his shirt. In the corridor, crates loaded for London. Son of Mounir and Sheila, named after the family friends who helped them, “
title: Lamine Yamal: ‘Football is mechanised but players like me have that special spark’

author: Mark Brown North of England correspondent
description:
Exclusive: Dog Painting 17 is believed to be one of only six of works from Dog Series in private hands and first to be auctioned

David Hockney adored his dachshunds Stanley and Boodgie and let them run riot – so much so that after one had an accident in the LA home of the actor Dennis Hopper, the painter is said to have quipped: “It’ll be dry in the morning, luv, and you can just pick it up.”

But Hockney did not just indulge his four-legged companions, he treated them as portrait subjects for a series of paintings, one of which is to be sold by Christie’s.

Continue reading...
title: Rare sale of David Hockney painting of beloved dog Stanley could fetch £2.5m

author: Zoe Williams
description:
The star chef demystified the restaurant scene with his love of a welcoming pub. Now he explains why hospitality is in crisis – and how to make a sublime venison chilli

Tom Kerridge is the king of meat: first as a chef, transforming pub classics like pork belly into Michelin-starred fare at The Hand and Flowers in Marlow 20 years ago, and later opening The Butcher’s Tap and Grill in the same village; then as a cookery writer: his Outdoor Cooking – The Ultimate Modern Barbecue Bible of 2021 is well named, being both as comprehensive and as worshipful as a holy book; and recently as a “meat-fluencer”, making gorgeous skills videos on Instagram and
title: Cooking with Tom Kerridge, the Michelin ‘meatfluencer’

author: Guardian Staff
description:
Daisy Edgar-Jones dons the bonnet in Georgia Oakley’s take on the Jane Austen classic, and Catherine Zeta-Jones battles assassins in a madcap action caper

Sense and Sensibility
Out now
Daisy Edgar-Jones has a big bonnet to fill in the role Emma Thompson made her own in Ang Lee’s Oscar-winning version of Jane Austen’s romance. But let’s not compare: Blue Jean director Georgia Oakley’s take sees a fresh cast place new emphasis on the bond between sisters Marianne and Elinor.

Continue reading...
title: From Sense and Sensibility to Kill Jackie: your complete entertainment guide to the week ahead

author: Jessica Elgot Deputy political editor
description:
The deputy leader wants the party to take advantage of a split on the right and not be embarrassed to show its values

Labour must “reunite the progressive voter coalition” if it is to take advantage of a split on the right and win the next election, the party’s deputy leader has said.

Lucy Powell, who won the race to be deputy leader 12 months ago with a warning that Labour was losing the fight to be heard as Reform UK surged, said the government now had a second chance under Andy Burnham.

Continue reading...
title: Labour must reunite progressive voters to win the next election, says Lucy Powell

author: Guardian Staff
description:
Miklos, 25, a PhD student, meets Minnie, 23, who works in film production

What were you hoping for?
To take a step outside my comfort zone. To meet the love of my life.

Continue reading...
title: Blind date: ‘I do wish I hadn’t stepped on that dog – but she assured me it was OK’

author: Nicola Davis Science correspondent
description:
New research suggests the technology could be used to increase out-of-hospital access to life-saving devices

Drones could help cut the time it takes to get a defibrillator to people experiencing cardiac arrests when not in hospital, researchers have suggested.

In the UK alone, there are more than 30,000 out-of-hospital cardiac arrests a year where emergency medical services attempt to resuscitate the individual, according to the British Heart Foundation. However, fewer than one in 10 people survive such an event, and some who do are left with neurological problems.

Continue reading...
title: Drones could speed up getting defibrillators to people having cardiac arrests, study suggests

author: Henry Harris
description:
A thick and creamy, flavourful onion soup topped with grated cheese and herbs

When I was a child, my mother often made onions in white sauce to serve with roast lamb. I loved their thick, velvety texture and how they brought richness, sweetness and even more savouriness to a good Sunday lunch. A similarly thick tangle of onions features in the classic soupe à l’oignon gratinée, which can’t really be mimicked without a deep, dark, beefy stock, so rather than even try, it’s best to introduce another layer of flavour entirely. The parsley here yields a very different end result that also proves to be rather comforting.

Henry Harris is chef/co-owner of Bouchon Racine, London EC1. His book, The Racine Effect, is published by Quadrille at £40. To order a copy for £36, go to guardianbookshop.com
title: Henry Harris’ vegetarian recipe for French onion and parsley soup

author: Anna Tims
description:
Despite guidance keeping mobile phones out of England’s schools, cheaper travel may only be available via an app

Schoolchildren who do not own smartphones face paying hundreds of pounds extra in annual bus fares as cheaper travel passes are digitised.

Critics argue that by only making discounts available through an app, operators are undermining government guidance to keep mobile phones out of schools.

Continue reading...
title: Schoolchildren without smartphones penalised with higher bus fares

author: Rowena Mason Whitehall editor
description:
From a difficult economic landscape to decisions on oil and gas drilling, welfare spending and the Chagos Islands, we look at what’s on the horizon

Andy Burnham is riding high ahead of the Labour party conference after a successful first meeting with Donald Trump, and with his party faithful excited by their uplift in the polls. He plans to bring a message of hope and optimism to the autumn gathering in Liverpool, and will benefit from goodwill among members as he makes his first speech as leader on Tuesday.

However, the real tests will start to land from October onwards, with a difficult economic landscape, the ongoing impact of the war in Iran and domestic challenges to navigate. Here is what Burnham has to look forward to after the conference is over.

Continue reading...
title: The tricky tests awaiting Andy Burnham after Labour conference

author: Rob Davies and Maxence Peigné
description:
Files could have seismic consequences for online casinos, including those accused of illegally targeting consumers

The secrets of thousands of online casinos have been laid bare in a vast leak of data that could have seismic consequences for offshore gambling firms, including some accused of illegally targeting consumers around the world.

The Casino Secrets leak reveals tens of thousands of previously confidential files stored by the gambling regulator on the Caribbean island of Curaçao.

Continue reading...
title: Vast Casino Secrets leak exposes inner workings of offshore gambling firms

author: David Conn
description:
Club’s ruthless approach was always at odds with their public image and this inglorious story has further to run

There is no episode in English football’s history that even resembles a precedent for the epic Manchester City disciplinary drama, which encapsulates the modern game at breaking point. Here was a grand, stoic old club, taken over in 2008 by Abu Dhabi royalty and mega-funded to imperious success, then crowned serial champions by a league simultaneously pursuing charges of monstrous financial cheating.

On Friday sources confirmed that saga, in which Pep Guardiola’s expensively constructed City teams won five Premier League titles and the Champions League during the years since the investigation began in December 2018, culminated in guilty findings on almost all of more than 100 charges.

Continue reading...
title: How drawn-out saga of Manchester City’s alleged cheating came to this

author: Jason Okundaye
description:
Even Jacob Rees-Mogg pushes back on defining Englishness in exclusively ethnic terms. But the endurance of this discourse is still deeply troubling

Can you be English and non-white? It’s a question that keeps stubbornly resurfacing in our political discourse.

Last weekend, the former prime minister Rishi Sunak gave his view in a column in the Times, arguing that national identity should not be turned into a DNA test. After leaving office, Sunak, the UK’s first prime minister of colour, was subject to claims by a prominent podcaster that he was not English because he was a “brown-skinned Hindu”. Reflecting on this, Sunak described it as a “reverse
title: Of course you can be English if you’re not white. So why can’t the right leave the question alone? | Jason Okundaye

description: Continue reading...

author: Tim Dowling
description:
My wife has summarily dismissed me from outdoor duties, in favour of ‘Gardening Steve’. Inevitably, there’s a catch

My wife wants to hire someone to put the garden in order. She knows I’ll object, because it’s really something I should be doing, but she also knows I won’t do it. In truth, I’ve lost heart. Two scorching months without rain wreaked havoc on the garden: the lawn turned the colour of a winter sky; seedlings vaporised; established shrubs died. When the rains finally came, the garden bounced back – but by then I didn’t care any more.

As part of her campaign my wife has let it be known that paying someone to fix the garden is no reflection on me, because I’m a businessman with little time to devote to things of the soil.

Continue reading...
title: Tim Dowling: I’ve been replaced by a younger model … it’s a relief

author: Samira Shackle
description:
When her parents waved her off to study in England they hoped it would be a fresh start the 16-year-old needed after struggling with her mental health in Hong Kong. Instead, 10 months later, she was dead. What went so wrong?

As a young teen, one of Luna Wong’s favourite things to do was to walk to a bridge near her home in Hong Kong and sit there for a while, listening to the traffic and the water below, looking out at the lights and the activity of the city. She had a particular way of observing the world, which she expressed through photography. Her pictures were mostly landscapes, ordinary corners of Hong Kong, but she could spot an image nobody else would have seen in the same place. She was an inquisitive kid who enjoyed making people laugh, and was deeply interested in the world around her. Then in 2019, when she was 13, political unrest in Hong Kong
title: ‘They accepted the money but didn’t take care of my child’: what Luna Wong’s death reveals about the treatment of international students in the UK

author: David Smith in Washington
description:
Outgoing secretary Lonnie Bunch rejects claims the institution is unpatriotic, telling audience ‘You cannot understand all without illuminating the dark corners’

Lonnie Bunch, the outgoing secretary of the Smithsonian Institution, has defended the organisation against political interference, insisting that telling the unvarnished and complex truths of history is an act of “great love” for the country.

Speaking on Friday at the National Museum of African American History and Culture in Washington, Bunch received a standing ovation from hundreds of audience members and rejected claims that the institution’s staff or exhibitions were unpatriotic.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Let’s tell the truth’: Smithsonian head given standing ovation as he hits back at Trump attacks

author: Agencies
description:
Trial had been set for Monday over claims by Alabama that TikTok misled parents about tools meant to shield children from harmful content

TikTok has agreed to pay Alabama at least $100m and enact time limits and other restrictions for teenage users, avoiding a trial with a settlement that was modelled on Instagram-owner Meta’s recent agreement with US states.

Alabama described it as a “first-in-the-nation settlement” with a state in the sweeping litigation over social media’s affect on teen wellbeing.

title: TikTok to pay Alabama $100m and limit teenage use in first state settlement

author: Juan A Ramírez
description:
The creators and stars of Slam Frank on their off-Broadway production - which reimagines the Holocaust victim as a pansexual rapper

It’s difficult to not invoke the term “woke” when discussing Slam Frank, the 2025 musical that reimagines Anne Frank as a pansexual Latina. Controversial even before its first performance, it giddily satirizes identity politics through its show-within-a-show structure, in which a progressive theatre company attempts to modernize the Holocaust victim’s story by paralleling it to the struggles faced by marginalized people today. Here, the mother of “Anita” is Black, her father is neurodivergent and, while hiding in Amsterdam, they are very much immigrants.

Creator Andrew Fox recognizes “a temptation to categorize it as anti-woke art”, but points readily at the show’s fans and detractors, who fall across every conceivable party line, and
title: ‘A couple of times people walked out’: how an Anne Frank musical became the hottest theater ticket of the year

author: Cas Mudde
description:
Defeatist narratives abound. Yet Germany’s latest elections suggest voter dissatisfaction is benefiting the left as well as the right

Germany held three regional elections this month and, although each of them had a unique result, much of the media and political commentary reduced them to: “German chancellor clings to power after latest loss to far right. Since 2016, the year of Brexit and Trump, “embattled mainstream threatened by emboldened far right” has become the overarching narrative about Europe. But while these elections were important, this reductive take both oversimplifies the complexities of contemporary European politics and drives a defeatist “
title: Look again – there’s more to Germany’s election trends than far-right success | Cas Mudde

author: Pjotr Sauer in Kyiv
description:
As winter approaches, Kyiv fears disruption to vital networks that keep banks, payment systems and public services running

  • Ukraine and Russia’s long-range drone war

Russia has opened a new front in its campaign against Ukraine, hitting several datacentres and internet providers in Kyiv this week in an apparent attempt to weaken the digital backbone of the economy.

About 100,000 households in Kyiv and the surrounding region suffered temporary internet outages after strikes on Wednesday and Thursday, according to Ukraine’s digital transformation ministry.

Continue reading...
title: Russia strikes at heart of Ukraine’s digital economy with attacks on ISPs and datacentres

author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
description:
Outlet had been scheduled to fly with Donald Trump to Tennessee for a college football game, network said Friday

The White House has blocked CNN from traveling aboard Air Force One on Saturday, impeding its TV press pool duties in the latest escalation of the administration’s battle with the news media.

CNN had been scheduled to fly with Donald Trump to Tennessee for a college football game, the network said on Friday. The White House confirmed CNN’s exclusion when it did not list the network on guidance sent to the press corps regarding Trump’s schedule for Saturday.

title: White House blocks CNN from Air Force One in latest escalation with news media
